title: Remarks at Cleveland, Tennessee
paragraphs: I thank you for having come out to greet me. We are making but a moment's stop and I shall merely express my acknowledgments and say what a pleasure it is to be here in your beautiful state-the.state of "Old Hickory", and a state that has ever taken a leading position both in peace and in war. Yesterday I enjoyed particularly going over the great battlefields. I feel that they are an inspiration for every good American to think of the deeds of valor done alike by the men who wore the blue and by those who wore the gray. I think we ought all to be better men for it, and I leave your state feeling, if possible, even a better American. (Cheers and applause)
